name: OrbitingCircles
description: Items that travel around a centre on one or more circular paths, such as the tools a product works with. The items are your own children and the orbit is plain CSS.

children.description: The items that orbit. Each child becomes one list item on a path.

center.description: Content placed in the middle of the paths, such as a logo or a heading.

radius.description: Radius of the outer path in pixels.

rings.description: How many paths. The children are shared out between them, and neighbouring paths turn in opposite directions.

duration.description: Seconds for one full turn of the outer path. Inner paths turn faster.

iconSize.description: Width and height of each item in pixels.

reverse.description: Turns the outer path the other way.

showPaths.description: Draws each path as a thin circle.

pauseOnHover.description: Pauses while the pointer is over the orbit or focus is inside it.

label.description: Accessible name of the list of items.

isPaused.description: Stops the orbit. Moving content that lasts more than five seconds should be stoppable.

keyboard: Tab: moves through any focusable item, in the order the children were given
requirements: The items are real children in a list, in a fixed DOM order, so the order never changes with the motion
The drawn paths are decoration: hidden from assistive technology and never take pointer events
The orbit is CSS only and starts after the page paints; the server HTML already shows the items spaced evenly
It can be stopped: isPaused, an optional pause on hover and focus, and the rdm-still class (WCAG 2.2.2)
Visitors who ask for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion) get the items evenly spaced and still
Items stay upright while they travel, so text and icons stay readable
In forced-colors (high contrast) mode the paths use a system colour
Does not flash: nothing changes more than three times in a second (WCAG 2.3.1)
screenReader: Announced as a list with the given label; each item is read in order as ordinary content

use_when: A hero section that shows the tools or integrations a product connects to
A small decorative diagram with a logo in the middle
avoid_when: Essential links that people must be able to hit easily, because moving targets are hard to use
More than about eight items on one path
anti_patterns: Putting the only way to reach a page on an orbiting item without pause on hover
A very short duration, which makes the items hard to follow
